title: A ball's de Broglie wavelength against atomic sizes
caption: For a 1 kg ball at 1 m s⁻¹, λ = h/p = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ m: about 23 orders of magnitude smaller than an atom (10⁻¹⁰ m) and 18 below a proton. No experiment can see wave behaviour at that scale. Electrons and atoms have wavelengths comparable with atomic sizes, which is why they diffract.
alt: A logarithmic length scale from 10^-35 m to 10^-8 m with the ball's de Broglie wavelength at 6.6 × 10^-34 m, far to the left of a proton at 1.7 × 10^-15 m and a hydrogen atom at 1.1 × 10^-10 m.
description: A horizontal logarithmic scale of length in metres.
The 1 kg ball at 1 m s⁻¹ has λ = h/p = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ m.
A proton is about 1.7 × 10⁻¹⁵ m across and a hydrogen atom about 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
The ball's wavelength is 23 orders of magnitude below the atom: far too small to measure, so the ball shows no wave behaviour.

claims.name: the ball's wavelength is 23 orders of magnitude below an atom
